headline: 5 Bangladeshis confirmed dead in Kolkata hotel fire
summary: At least nine people died in the blaze; victims include a journalist and three family members from Kushtia.
details: A devastating fire at a residential hotel in Kolkata, India, has left at least nine people dead, including five confirmed Bangladeshi citizens.
The identities of the victims were confirmed by Mohammad Khaled, the Deputy High Commissioner of Bangladesh in Kolkata, on Wednesday.
Among the deceased Bangladeshis, four are residents of Kushtia and one is from Dhaka.
Reports indicate that a journalist and three family members from Kushtia were among those who perished in the blaze.
The hotel's safety standards have come under scrutiny, with reports highlighting narrow staircases and a lack of emergency exits.
This tragedy follows another hotel fire in West Bengal within just two days, which also resulted in eight deaths.

Among the deceased Bangladeshis, four are residents of Kushtia and one is from Dhaka.

Reports indicate that a journalist and three family members from Kushtia were among those who perished in the blaze.

The hotel's safety standards have come under scrutiny, with reports highlighting narrow staircases and a lack of emergency exits.

This tragedy follows another hotel fire in West Bengal within just two days, which also resulted in eight deaths.

headline_marked: 30 injured as [[madrasa students clash with police]] in Brahmanbaria
headline: 30 injured as madrasa students clash with police in Brahmanbaria
summary: The clash erupted after students from Darul Arkam Islamia Madrasa protested against a cultural program organized by the district police.
details: At least 30 people, including seven police officers, were injured in a clash between madrasa students and police in Brahmanbaria on Tuesday night.
The incident occurred around 11:30 PM at the Police Lines field's drill shed in the West Medda area of the city.
Students from Darul Arkam Islamia Madrasa protested against a cultural program held by the district police, citing objections to loud music.
The situation escalated when over 100 students entered the Police Lines, vandalized chairs, and threw bricks, leading police to use batons to control the crowd.
Following the clash, students held protests on various city roads and at the Press Club, demanding justice for the injured and a ban on concerts.
District Council Administrator Sirajul Islam and Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh Secretary General Sajidur Rahman mediated a meeting to calm the situation.
According to Sajidur Rahman, the police have agreed to all their demands, and the Superintendent of Police (SP) stated that three police officers in charge would be dismissed.
The injured students were treated at Brahmanbaria General Hospital.
The DB OC of the district police confirmed that the students entered through the pocket gate and vandalized the venue before police intervened.
caption:
30 people injured after madrasa students clashed with police over a cultural program in Brahmanbaria.

At least 30 people, including seven police officers, were injured in a clash between madrasa students and police in Brahmanbaria on Tuesday night.

The incident occurred around 11:30 PM at the Police Lines field's drill shed in the West Medda area of the city.

Students from Darul Arkam Islamia Madrasa protested against a cultural program held by the district police, citing objections to loud music.

The situation escalated when over 100 students entered the Police Lines, vandalized chairs, and threw bricks, leading police to use batons to control the crowd.

Following the clash, students held protests on various city roads and at the Press Club, demanding justice for the injured and a ban on concerts.

District Council Administrator Sirajul Islam and Hefazat-e-Islam Bangladesh Secretary General Sajidur Rahman mediated a meeting to calm the situation.

According to Sajidur Rahman, the police have agreed to all their demands, and the Superintendent of Police (SP) stated that three police officers in charge would be dismissed.

The injured students were treated at Brahmanbaria General Hospital.

The DB OC of the district police confirmed that the students entered through the pocket gate and vandalized the venue before police intervened.
